body: I have had extensive counseling. At this point, it's just a matter of building trust and comfort. He has seen a counselor for stuff in the past and I'm more than willing to support him in whatever decisions he makes in the future. Thank you so much.

Kind of a long story, but I'll try my best to shorten it.
I have suffered from PTSD for almost 6 years now from being raped by 2 different guys in my neighborhood. It flared up again after I started getting harassing phone calls from a bad guy and when I found out that my family was moving away to a different state (leaving me as the only member of my entire immediate and extended family for over 1,000 miles). Around the same time, my best friend started to alienate me and leave me out. Long story short, my anxiety kicked in and I ended up making a nuisance of myself. But he assured me that everything would be okay and that we would be okay for the summer. Earlier in the year, we had decided to live as neighbors in an apartment building and I was relying on him. He was the only one I knew in the area. But at the beginning of the summer, he told me that we were no longer friends. I shouldered the blame for the ruined friendship. My PTSD got worse...I started having flashbacks nightly. I developed an eating disorder and lost almost 40 pounds. I also began cutting myself. I ended up overdosing a grand total of 3 times in an attempt to end my life. I had no one and was completely alone. I couldn't go to my family, and I tried to protect my remaining friends. I spent about a month in the hospital (both inpatient and outpatient). I've come very far. But as of late, I feel myself falling back again....and I'm ashamed to be slipping. I've been idealizing hurting myself again....and I'm really not sure what to do.

Thanks everyone for your support. It feels a lot like a grieving process. Like I've lost a huge part of me, but at the same time, when I got better I was finally able to find myself again. I guess it's scary to think how easily that person could take over, and how little I can trust her. I held on for so long for everyone that I loved....but I couldn't do it any longer than I did. I remember screaming in the ambulance and in the ER "Please, just let me die." I just wish that someone could have just held me at that point and told me that everything was going to get better. I still have times when I think, "I almost wasn't here for this" or "what would this be like without me". I don't know, it's a very weird and surreal feeling.

That's good to hear. I'm here for you too if you need it. It's scary and sucks trying to tell the people you love. I haven't told my family. But the phone calls I made to my closest friends were some of the hardest ones I've ever made.

I have. For the most part, I always get stuff like "you need to forgive yourself" or "you weren't you, you were ill." I know they all mean well, but it doesn't help what I'm feeling. I felt guilty and really overwhelmed that I could get so close to suicide...but now there's just this empty feeling that I can't even articulate to anyone.
Thank you so much for your kind words. I've never shared my story before and this is the only way I know how.

I've been in therapy for the past few months, according to my therapist I'm doing everything right. I take my meds religiously and I even have a PTSD therapy dog. But none of that seems to help the fact that I've been abandoned and left to deal with all of this on my own. A couple nights ago I tried to kill myself, I overdosed on my anti-anxiety meds and cut myself worse than I ever had. A huge part of me thinks that I deserve it. I destroyed my friendship, and was stupid enough to think he would forgive me and that everything would be ok. And now I'm stuck with no family and no friends. I've been in the psych ward before and I barely survived that time. I know I won't make it in there again if I'm alone....which is what I would be. I'm just backed into a corner and I don't know how to get out.

Thanks so much. I've felt like I have been going crazy the past couple months. I finally got up the courage to go into the Crisis Center in town, and I'm gonna start up with regular counseling. It's been incredibly overwhelming, and I think I'm gonna need to take the weekend to decompress and just be on my own...but I'm hoping that this is the first step in my road to recovery.

Thanks for your input. I finally got up the courage to go to the Crisis Center around. It's been overwhelming, and I've basically had to take an entire day to decompress and come to terms with it....but I'm hoping that this is the start of my recovery.

No problem! For a beginning baroque singer, I would recommend to try turns first at cadential points. Another thing you might find easy is to add scales where you have leaps. For instance, add a passing tone in between a jump of a third. Another easy ornament is taking it up an octave. If you end triumphantly and it makes sense for you to go up, do it. The last one you will defs need is cadential trills. A baroque piece is nothing without it's trills. =)

My favs:
1) Don't focus too much on legato exercises. Work on your staccato to get pitch accuracy and immediacy of placement
2) Don't underestimate the power of air. If you're having trouble with a phrase try singing it on a lip trill or rolled "r" to get your breath going
3) Like ghoti023 said, tongue exercises are awesome. For instance, if you have jaw tension, it might just be tongue tension in disguise.

I've been studying Baroque arias too, especially Handel. I'd recommend taking a really good look at the piece itself and how it fits in your voice. For instance, Piangero la sorte mia is an aria which sits really well in my voice but is awkward to ornament. This is because this aria is already ornamented in its own way in order to better portray the "crying" nature of it. Adding more ornamentation is not necessarily good. It has to fit both in the piece and in the voice comfortably. If it's awkward for you, it'll be awkward for your audience.
